title: Lester at Phillips's home; Booker takes them to Freddie Wood's
summary: Lester knew Phillips's wife Evelyn, married in 1934; they went on to Freddie Wood's at 17th and U where Paul Jones and Red Elkins were.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: No, Prez! Yeah, he knew my wife.
That's the wife you showed me in the picture.
You got married in what year?
So she came to D.C. with you.

Yeah, she came here with me. We came together. In fact, she came here before I did. I sent her here first because I knew I was coming. I sent her here first and she got everything straightened out. Then we said, "Come on, man. We got a place we gonna take you." Booker said, "Yeah." Because, see, Booker was up there playing, too, in... He had been sitting around playing a little bit up in this jam session we played. So Booker said, "Yeah, let's go up there, man." Booker said, "This is the cat I've been wanting to hear! Because Phil and them always about you, man. He said,

"You'all good friends, aren't you." He said, "Yeah, we just like brothers. Pete's my brother-in-law." You know what I mean? He said, "We're just like brothers." Booker said, "Yeah? Well, they're always talking about they want us to hear you." And Booker said, "I'm gonna hear you tonight." He laughed.

Then we got in the car and went on up to Freddie Wood's, up there at 17th and U. So we went up there, and Paul Jones said... See, they were playing at the Bluebird. We all got there about the same time.
